\section{Symbolic outputs for the surveyed theories}%
\label{SymbolicOutputs}

% Per-theory equation/constraint/term counts used in figure captions.
% Auto-generated by scripts/listings/compute_appendix_counts.py.
\input{sections/appendices/listings/counts.tex}

The theories below are presented under a common reduction: each is
linearised around its own background and then dimensionally reduced
to plane waves propagating along $\hat{z}$ (\cref{Linearisation}).
The surveyed-theory campaigns initialise the gravitational wave on
the cross polarisation $h_{xy}$, i.e.\ the Gertsenshtein channel
$h_\times \!\leftrightarrow\! a_\parallel$, whose conversion product
is the photon component $A_x$ at the rate
$\sin^{2}(\kappa \Bzero\,t / 2)$ familiar from the Boccaletti
formula (\cref{Validation}). To keep the displayed listings
readable, the longer ones show the equations of motion for this
channel together with the equations of motion for any torsion
components that couple into them (so the displayed sub-system is
dynamically closed); equations of motion for the orthogonal
polarisation, gauge modes, and the uncoupled constraint sub-block
are computed by the pipeline but pruned from the figures below.

Hamiltonian densities are presented as the self-GW + self-EM
sector relevant to the conversion measurement: torsion-coupled
terms are dropped at emission and cross-sector
$h_{\mu\nu}\!\otimes\!A_{\mu}$ interaction terms are excluded
from the rendered density, so the displayed
$\mathscr{H} \supset \dots$ is a proper subset of the full
canonical density (cf.\ \cref{DiracBergmann}).

Each theory is also accompanied by its linearised kinetic
matrix $\mathcal{K}(\partial_t, \partial_z)$ of
\cref{KineticMatrix} --- the wave-operator matrix from
$\lag^{(2)} = \tfrac{1}{2}\xi^\mathsf{T}\mathcal{K}\xi$
collapsed into a single display. The matrix exposes the channel
structure at a glance: diagonal entries carry the kinetic,
gradient, and mass terms per field; off-diagonal entries are the
inter-field couplings. Theories with velocity-pair fields admit
first-time-derivative contributions on the RHS; these appear as
additional columns labelled $\dot{X}$ for each q-field $X$
whose velocity is referenced. The matrix therefore acts on the
augmented state vector $\Xi = (q, \dot{q})^\mathsf{T}$ for those
theories, and the rendered matrix is rectangular
($n_{\mathrm{eq}} \times (n_q + n_v)$). Reading the matrix as a
system: row $i$ contracted with $\Xi$ gives equation $i$ in the
form $\mathcal{K}_{ij}\Xi_j = 0$.

% --- E.1  Einstein--Maxwell Gertsenshtein baseline ------------------
\subsection{Einstein--Maxwell Gertsenshtein baseline}%
\label{SymbolicBaseline}
Linearised around a uniform magnetic background
$\bm{B} = \Bzero\,\hat{x}$. The pure Einstein--Maxwell Lagrangian
gives a block-diagonal kinetic sub-matrix in the transverse photon
channels of \cref{BaselineKineticOutput}; discussed in
\cref{Validation}.

% --- E.3  Minimally-coupled Einstein--Cartan ------------------------
\subsection{Minimally-coupled Einstein--Cartan}%
\label{SymbolicReference}
Linearised around a uniform magnetic background
$\bm{B} = \Bzero\,\hat{x}$. Three quadratic torsion invariants with
couplings $\beta_{1,2,3}$ are added to Einstein--Maxwell; no
curvature-squared or nonminimal terms appear, and the torsion
components enter only in equations with LHS $=0$
(\cref{ReferenceKineticOutput}); discussed in \cref{SectorSurvey}.

% --- E.4  Propagating PGT with the curvature-squared term -----------
\subsection{Propagating PGT with the curvature-squared term}%
\label{SymbolicMechanism}
Linearised around a uniform magnetic background
$\bm{B} = \Bzero\,\hat{x}$. The $\Alp{1}\MAGFt{}^{2}$
curvature-squared term promotes the metric-perturbation sector to
a fourth-order system. We include this theory \emph{for
inspection} of the resulting equation-of-motion structure rather
than as part of the simulated-theory campaign: the $\Alp{1}$-weighted
contributions land only on the diagonal $h_{ii}$ kinetic equations
(see the $2\,\Alp{1}\,\partial_t^{4}h_{xx}$ representative displayed
in \cref{PropagatingKineticOutput}) and are absent from the
off-diagonal $h_{xy}$ equation that mediates the Gertsenshtein
channel $h_\times \!\leftrightarrow\! a_\parallel$. Linear-order
$h_{xy}\!\leftrightarrow\!A_{x}$ conversion is therefore
unaffected by the $\Alp{1}$ coupling, a null result we read directly
from the equations rather than confirm by simulation; discussed in
\cref{SectorSurvey}.

The Hamiltonian density is suppressed for this figure. The
fourth-order time derivatives lie outside the domain of v6's
no-Ostrogradsky-reduction policy, no published constraint-
promotion Hamiltonian recipe exists for the
$\Alp{1} \MAGFt{}^{2}$ case (Blagojevi\'c and Cvetkovi\'c
2018, App.\,D), and the pipeline's
\verb|ParseHamiltonianExpression| filter does not cover the
4th-order sector. The partial expression the pipeline emits for
this theory is preserved as a comment in the listing file for
reference but is not rendered.

\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\adjustbox{max width=\linewidth}{$\displaystyle
\setlength{\jot}{1pt}%
\begin{gathered}
\input{sections/appendices/listings/eom_mechanism_full.tex}
\end{gathered}
$}
\caption{Propagating-torsion PGT with parameter $\Alp{1}$ on
$\bm{B} = \Bzero\,\hat{x}$, plane-wave-reduced along $\hat{z}$.
Full pipeline output: \MechanismEomCount{} equations of motion
(\MechanismConstraintCount{} constraints),
\MechanismTermCount{} RHS terms. $\mathscr{H}$ suppressed ---

% --- E.5  Ricci--EM nonminimal coupling -----------------------------
\subsection{Ricci--EM nonminimal coupling}%
\label{SymbolicNonminimal}
Linearised around a uniform magnetic background
$\bm{B} = \Bzero\,\hat{x}$. A single new vertex
$\delta_{1}\MAGFt{_{\mu\nu}}\FieldA{^{\mu\nu}}$ is added to the
Einstein--Cartan terms (\cref{NonminimalKineticOutput}). The
$\delta_{1}$ coupling generates entries in every $h_{\mu\nu}$
equation and second-time-derivative entries in the torsion
sector; discussed in \cref{SectorSurvey}.

% --- E.6  Full YM--PGT nonminimal -----------------------------------
\subsection{Full YM--PGT nonminimal}%
\label{SymbolicGeneralNonminimal}
Linearised around a uniform magnetic background
$\bm{B} = \Bzero\,\hat{x}$. The full Yang--Mills-form Poincar\'e
gauge Lagrangian turns on $\beta_{1,2,3}$, $\xi$, $\delta_{1}$,
$\chi$, $\zeta_{1,2,3}$ simultaneously. The Bahamonde, Barker,
and Shapiro variants of \cref{SectorSurvey} are parameter
restrictions of the same Lagrangian; the surveyed system is
collected in \cref{GeneralNonminimalKineticOutput}; discussed in
\cref{SectorSurvey}.

% --- E.7  Parity-odd extension --------------------------------------
\subsection{Parity-odd extension}%
\label{SymbolicParityOdd}
Linearised around a uniform magnetic background
$\bm{B} = \Bzero\,\hat{x}$. $d_{14}$--$d_{17}$,
$d_{19}$--$d_{21}$, and $\zeta_{1}$--$\zeta_{6}$ are added to the
full Yang--Mills-form Lagrangian
(\cref{ParityOddKineticOutput}); discussed in \cref{SectorSurvey}.

Under the self-sector restriction of \cref{DiracBergmann}, the
rendered Hamiltonian density for this theory is byte-identical
to the YM--PGT Hamiltonian shown in
\cref{GeneralNonminimalKineticOutput}. This is expected: the
parity-odd invariants contribute only to cross-sector
$h_{\mu\nu}\!\otimes\!A_{\mu}$ interaction terms --- which the
self-sector filter removes --- and to an additional constraint
equation, which is suppressed alongside
the rest of the constraint sub-block. The self-energy diagonal
sector itself is unchanged.

% --- E.8  Dark-photon-plasma analogue -------------------------------
\subsection{Dark-photon-plasma analogue}%
\label{SymbolicDarkPhotonPlasma}
Linearised around a uniform magnetic background
$\bm{B} = \Bzero\,\hat{x}$. A kinetic-mixing vertex
$\delta_{m}\,F_{\mu\nu}\tilde{F}^{\mu\nu}$ (with $\tilde{F}$ the
torsion-trace field strength) and a photon mass term
$m_{A}^{2}$ are added to the Einstein--Cartan Lagrangian.
$m_{A}^{2}$ enters the diagonal photon kinetic term;
$\delta_{m}$ enters the off-diagonal photon--torsion entries
(\cref{DarkPhotonPlasmaKineticOutput}); discussed in
\cref{SectorSurvey}.
